# Climate Sprints

> A principal-led advisory practice for capital allocating into climate. We assess
> whether the technology works and whether anyone is compelled to buy it, then stay
> to fix what the assessment found.

Buyers are fund managers, family offices, LPs and industrial-scale developers.
The companies they fund are the beneficiaries, not the buyers.

## Pages
- [Diligence](https://climatesprints.com/diligence): Technical readiness, commercial compulsion and execution capacity, assessed together. Three weeks, fixed fee, opening with a paid definition phase.
- [Portfolio](https://climatesprints.com/portfolio): Momentum Sprints, Alignment Sprints, the Mastermind and fractional executives, bought by the fund and delivered to the company.
- [Momentum Sprints](https://climatesprints.com/momentum): Three months, from a technology that works to a buyer who is compelled.
- [Alignment Sprints](https://climatesprints.com/alignment): The execution risk more capital cannot fix. Led by Iana Lahi.
- [Fractional and interim executives](https://climatesprints.com/fractional): A senior seat filled in weeks, without a search.
- [Climate Catalyst Mastermind](https://climatesprints.com/mastermind): Twelve-week peer cohort for portfolio CEOs. First cohort 1Q2027. Runs on AGGEIO.
- [Approach](https://climatesprints.com/approach): The position, the sectors, the screen and the values.
- [Practice](https://climatesprints.com/practice): Founding principal Marc Strauch, and the standing bench.
- [Conversations](https://climatesprints.com/conversations): Recorded conversations. No cadence, no episode count.
- [Questions](https://climatesprints.com/questions): Fees, conflicts, ownership of the assessment, NDAs, and what the practice does not do.
- [Contact](https://climatesprints.com/contact)
- [Colophon](https://climatesprints.com/colophon): On the USGS imagery and the typefaces.

## The published method
- [/method](https://climatesprints.com/method): The assessment method in full and open — four assessments, twenty-four scored dimensions, the question behind each, the evidence that satisfies it, the A to D evidence grading scheme, the divergence patterns, and the kill criteria. Published so it can be argued with.
- [/origin](https://climatesprints.com/origin): The 1999 industrial-scale battery storage position the method was built out of, published under the founding principal's name.

The method itself is open and published in full on /method. The documents built on it are
available on request rather than as public downloads, in two parallel editions:

- **Allocator edition** — the method as it is run: what each of the twenty-four dimensions asks,
  the evidence that satisfies it, the scale anchors, the grading scheme, and the rule for what
  happens when two assessments disagree. Written for the person underwriting the position.
- **Founder edition** — the same twenty-four dimensions from the other side of the table: what an
  allocator is testing, what an answer reveals when the evidence is absent, and what to fix before
  a raise. Written for the company being assessed.

Neither is a summary of the other. Requested through the form on any page; the link arrives by
email and is good for seven days.

## Definitions
Terms used on this site with a specific meaning:

- **Commercial compulsion**: whether a named buyer, at a named organization, is obliged to act on a dateable timeline — as distinct from whether a market exists or is large.
- **Timing bet**: a position where the technology works and no buyer is compelled to act on any date that can be named. Legitimate, and mispriced when it is not sized as one.
- **Evidence grade**: a letter, A to D, recorded against every score, describing where the evidence came from rather than how favorable it was. A is an independent third party with no position in the outcome; D is company assertion, and caps the score at 3 regardless of the claim.
- **Execution capacity**: whether a founding team can move a working technology to a compelled buyer inside the capital and the time available. Scored across eight dimensions from observed behavior, never from documents and never by a tool.
- **The dated comparison**: the date a buyer becomes compelled set against the month the company's cash runs out. Reported as one finding rather than two scores.
- **Capital readiness**: what backing a company actually commits an allocator to — total capital to breakeven, dilution to exit, and whether the runway reaches a milestone a later investor treats as de-risking. Treated as a gate, not averaged against the other three.
- **Unit economics at scale**: what the second unit costs and what makes it cheaper than the first, with the decline attributed to named causes rather than an assumed percentage. The implied learning rate is stated as a number and set against the 10–20% band observed across complex industrial deployment.
